It has been procedure for years to notify local shipping about difficult ice before they actually enter such areas so appropriate bridge decisions can made. The primary area of interest is within 59°45’N-62°00N and 42°50’W-48°30’W. The standard products based on the helicopter recce are the following: - Ice report in plain language - Photo series of ice conditions at selected or critical positions or annotated satellite imagery. Most often .jpg files with symbols and explanations of ice conditions. - Direct ice advisory to ships via HF radio Satellite data recorded in visual wavelength in resolutions of 15-20 m or better are very valuable for the inshore mapping program however fog, cloud cover and winter darkness is a significant limitation and imagery recorded with Synthetic Aperture Radar is a necessary complimentary datasource.
